## 1. Unicycle linearised at rest

A = 0, B(theta) = [[cos th, 0], [sin th, 0], [0, 1]] -> rank C = **2** of 3 (not controllable: no instantaneous lateral motion).

## 3. Local observability of the EKF model

| sensors | motion | rank O | unobservable direction (x, y, theta) |
|---|---|---|---|
| odometry only | moving | 0 | all |
| 1 marker [r, b] | static | 2 | [-0.22, +0.87, -0.44] |
| 1 marker [r, b] | moving | 2 | [+0.22, -0.87, +0.44] |
| 1 marker [r, b, alpha] | static | 3 | - |
| 2 markers [r, b] | static | 3 | - |

With a single point landmark measured in range and bearing the unobservable direction is a rotation of the robot's pose about the landmark (position moves along the circle around the marker and the heading turns by the same angle). Odometry is expressed in the body frame, so this rotation leaves every future measurement unchanged: **motion does not remove it**. The PnP relative heading alpha (the marker's orientation is known in the map) or a second marker does. This is why the dock approach uses z = [r, b, alpha] when the marker is large enough in the image, and why the room has extra wall markers. Odometry alone observes nothing absolute: the covariance grows without bound until a marker is seen (see the estimation plots / odom_only scenario).
